errors.note: WITHDRAWN, enrollment 0. whyStopped: 'No Participants Enrolled'. I labelled this not_stated because the text only restates the withdrawn/zero-enrollment status and gives no cause. Stored enrollment_feasibility reads it as a recruitment failure. The text supports either reading, so the stored label is acceptable, not wrong. Other axes match.

TERMINATED, 13 enrolled. whyStopped is empty, but the record's briefSummary states: 'The trial was terminated because of difficulties in identifying patients who met the eligibility criteria.' That is a stated recruitment/eligibility feasibility reason, so stored not_stated is wrong. Its evidence ('no stated reason for stopping') suggests the labeler saw only the whyStopped field and not the description module. This is an input-scope gap. Labels from records that give the reason only in the description text are biased toward not_stated. Execution, endpoint (no results), safety (unknown) and efficacy_failure (false) match.

WITHDRAWN, enrollment 0; whyStopped 'Sponsor decision to cancel trial, not related to safety concern.' Safety: the stored label is none_evident and mine is unknown. With zero participants there is no safety data, but the record explicitly rules out a safety reason ('not related to safety concern'), so none_evident is defensible. Both labels mean 'not notable', so downstream use is unaffected.

WITHDRAWN, enrollment 0; whyStopped 'Protocol redundancy', meaning another study made this one redundant (replaced_by_new_protocol; 'other' would be the only alternative). Safety: the stored label is none_evident and mine is unknown. Nobody was enrolled, and unlike NCT05726682 the record says nothing about safety. The labeler gave unknown to the equivalent zero-enrollment records NCT01305551 and NCT06052423, so this label is inconsistent with its own practice. It is still defensible because the record shows no safety problem, and both values mean 'not notable'.

This is the one trial where the labels differ. The stored label is not_met with efficacy_failure=true; mine is not_assessable with efficacy_failure=false. The study is single-arm and open-label, with primary outcome 'ORR per RECIST 1.1 by Central Assessment': Cohort 1 5.9% (CI 1.6-14.4, n=68), Cohort 2 11.1% (CI 2.4-29.2, n=27). The record posts no statistical analysis and no prespecified null or success threshold for ORR, so 'a negative result on the primary objective' cannot be read directly from it. I treated the result as descriptive. Reading a 5.9% ORR in the main cohort as a negative efficacy result is still defensible, so not_met is acceptable. The stored efficacy_failure=true follows consistently from not_met in a trial with an efficacy primary. I marked it correct only because the binary verdict has no 'acceptable' option; my own value was false. On safety, there are 53/68 and 20/27 deaths over 38 months in advanced HCC with no comparator arm, so no excess can be shown and none_evident matches.

The stored label is mixed; mine is not_assessable. The primary outcome (change in weekly SBMs, 3 arms) has no analysis or p-value posted, only means with SE: 0.25 mg 3.42 (0.49), 0.1 mg 1.96 (0.35), placebo 1.44 (0.27). The rubric's 'met' requires statistical significance, which the record never shows, so I chose not_assessable. Mixed is still defensible. Inferred from the SEs, 0.25 mg sits about 3.5 SE above placebo and 0.1 mg about 1.2 SE above, i.e. one dose separated and one did not. The stored evidence says it inferred this from spread. Safety: SAEs 2/45 (MI, COPD) on 0.25 mg vs 0 elsewhere and no deaths, which is not a clear excess.

TERMINATED, 26 enrolled (tozadenant abuse-potential crossover). whyStopped: 'New Safety Information'. No results posted. The safety stop reason makes the signal notable under the rubric. All axes match.

TERMINATED, 22 enrolled. whyStopped: 'Phase 1completed; sponsor decided to change strategy to a combination study' (a strategic decision, so business_portfolio). Results are posted. The only primary outcome is descriptive Phase 1 safety (DLT 1, TEAEs 18, SAEs 9, IRRs 10 of 22) with no analyses, so not_assessable. The single arm has 3 deaths and 9 SAE patients out of 22 in advanced solid tumours. The SAEs are scattered single events, mostly disease-related (bile duct and bowel obstruction, malignant progression). With no comparator arm and only 1 DLT, no excess is evident. Stored secondary_reasons (replaced_by_new_protocol, objectives_met_or_early_success) are reasonable. All scored axes match.

TERMINATED, 92 enrolled (Phase 3 riboflavin/KXL cross-linking vs placebo). There is no whyStopped field, and neither the brief summary nor any other text gives a reason. No results are posted. All axes match.

TERMINATED after enrolling 49 (24 and 25 in two single-arm TAK-659 cohorts); whyStopped 'Lack of efficacy of the drug; no safety concern'. The Stage 2 IRRC ORR primary outcome is posted with denominators of 0, and the population note says 'study was terminated before the initiation of Stage 2, data was not collected', so it is not_assessable. Safety: deaths 3/24 and 3/25 and SAEs 14/24 and 13/25 in relapsed/refractory DLBCL, with no control arm to show an excess, and the stop reason explicitly says 'no safety concern', so none_evident. efficacy_failure is true because of the efficacy_futility stop. All stored labels match.

TERMINATED after enrolling 23 in a Phase 1 first-in-human trial of the CDK2 inhibitor NKT3447; whyStopped 'This study was terminated as a result of Sponsor portfolio reprioritization.' No results. All stored labels match.

All axes match. whyStopped: 'sponsor decision due to low recruitment'. The IDMC called the study 'futile' because of slow recruitment, not because of efficacy. The ARR rate ratio was 1.270 (p=0.5252), but limitations say 'the insufficient sample size did not allow to detect the differences for the main efficacy endpoints', so not_assessable fits better than not_met. No arm had excess deaths or SAEs: ponesimod 0 deaths and 6/67 SAE, placebo 1 death and 7/68 SAE.
All axes match. Status TERMINATED with 14 enrolled. The whyStopped field and detailed description are empty, and no results are posted.

All axes match, though two labels rest on inference. (1) whyStopped says 'terminated early by the Sponsor following the prespecified interim analysis for sample size re-estimation at approximately 75% enrollment' and never uses the word futility. Reading it as efficacy_futility by meaning is defensible, and other or sponsor_decision_unspecified would also be arguable. (2) No statistical analysis is posted for the primary endpoint, only LS means for MADRS change at Day 28: -14.81 (SE 1.00) vs -13.9 (SE 1.01). A 0.9-point gap with these SEs is clearly non-significant, so not_met is reasonable; not_assessable would also be defensible. SAEs were 0/119 vs 0/117 with no deaths.

All axes match. whyStopped: 'Data did not show that the two biologic treatments impacted PMR disease activity to the same degree as steroid treatment'. PMR-AS percent reduction was 64.5 for ACZ885 (n=3), 51.7 for AIN457 (n=6) and 91.9 for prednisone (n=4), with no formal test posted. The sponsor's own statement is a negative result on the primary objective. There were no SAEs or deaths in any arm, and 1 AE discontinuation on ACZ885.

All axes match. whyStopped: 'Enough data has been collected to allow analysis of safety profile and risk-benefit.' That is closest to objectives met, though 'other' would be arguable. 13 were enrolled and no results are posted.

All axes match. whyStopped says only 'Ended prematurely', which gives no reason. The primary PD outcome, change in anti-FXa activity, is reported descriptively only: andexanet -23.45 and -26.17 vs placebo -1.67 and -2.17 ug/L, with no statistical comparison, so not_assessable applies. SAEs were 0 in all arms.
All axes match. whyStopped: 'Trial terminated early per business decision.' One participant was enrolled, so this is stopped_early rather than withdrawn. No results are posted.
All axes match. Status WITHDRAWN with ACTUAL enrollment 0. whyStopped is empty and no results are posted.

All axes match. whyStopped: 'Business Reasons'. 296 were enrolled. hasResults is false: primary completion was 2025-11-05 and no results section exists, so no_results and unknown safety are correct from the registry.

All axes match. whyStopped: 'Sponsor elected not to continue with study', with no further reason. The Part A primary outcome was 14.3% complete responders (1 of 7) in a single arm, with no prespecified success threshold or analysis posted. Part B is descriptive safety only, so not_assessable applies. SAEs were 0/9 with no deaths.

All axes match. Status COMPLETED, n=24. Both primary Emax-model outcomes favour DFV890 over placebo at every dose. IL-6: 10 mg p=0.0011, 25-100 mg p<0.0001. IL-18: 10 mg p=0.0108, 25 mg p=0.0007, 50/100 mg p<0.0001. No deaths. The only serious AEs were 2 in the 50 mg arm (n=10): one transient ischaemic attack and one nephrolithiasis. That is not a clear excess.

All axes match. Status COMPLETED, n=169. Primary outcome, TETRAS composite change at week 17: LS mean difference -1.06 [-2.83, 0.70], p=0.2363 (MMRM), so not_met and efficacy_failure=true. Serious AEs were 4/83 on drug vs 2/86 on placebo, with scattered terms (dysphagia, fall, CVA, anxiety, vertebral fracture) and no deaths. That is not a clear excess.

All axes match. Phase 3, n=180. Week 48 HBV DNA <50 IU/mL plus HBeAg seroconversion: entecavir 24.4% vs placebo 2.4%, difference 20.2 (9.1-31.4), p=0.0049. Serious AEs were 4/120 on entecavir vs 9/60 on placebo, with no deaths.

All axes match. The only primary outcome is a descriptive safety count, 'Number of Participants With Drug-related AEs of Grade 3 or Higher': 20/40. That makes it not_assessable, with efficacy_failure=false. I call safety notable because the record attributes grade 3+ toxicity to the drug in 50% of participants. Serious AEs were 26/40, including immune-related colitis (3), hypophysitis (3), adrenal insufficiency (3), pneumonitis (4) and intestinal perforation. Note that the stored evidence also cites 35/40 deaths. Those deaths come from 5-year follow-up in a single-arm recurrent ovarian cancer trial and are not by themselves a drug signal. The notable label stands on the drug-related grade 3+ rate instead.
All axes match. Extension study, n=5. The primary outcome is the number of participants with AEs (4/5), which is purely descriptive safety. There were 0 deaths and 0 serious AEs.

All axes match. CheckMate 274, n=709. Both primary DFS outcomes were met: ITT HR 0.70 (0.55-0.90), p=0.0008; PD-L1>=1% HR 0.54 (0.35-0.84), p=0.0005. Serious AEs were 122/351 on nivolumab vs 129/348 on placebo. All-cause mortality is blinded in the record.

All axes match. The co-primary efficacy endpoints at week 16 split. Tanezumab 5 mg was significant vs NSAID on WOMAC pain (p=0.0148) and WOMAC function (p=0.0030) but not on PGA (p=0.3431). Tanezumab 2.5 mg was significant on none of the three (p=0.1597, 0.0691, 0.6332). That makes the endpoint mixed, and efficacy_failure=false is consistent with the rubric. Safety is notable: the primary composite joint safety outcome was 3.9% and 7.1% on tanezumab vs 1.5% on NSAID (p=0.0123, p<0.0001), and serious AEs were 80/998 at 5 mg vs 46/996 on NSAID.

All axes match. The single-arm ORR primary was met: Phase 1b + Phase 2 ORR 50.0% vs a prespecified null of 30%, exact binomial p=0.0076. The Phase 1b DLT primary is descriptive (1 DLT). On safety, there were 23/38 deaths, 28/38 serious AEs and 15/38 serious pneumonia in triple-class-refractory myeloma, with no comparator and no stated safety problem. I agree with none_evident, though notable could be argued from the pneumonia rate.

All axes match. The record posts no statistical analysis for the primary outcome (MAS change at week 4). The means and SDs are placebo -0.3 (0.6), 500 U -1.2 (1.0) and 1000 U -1.4 (1.1), with n≈80 per arm, which gives roughly t≈7 for 500 U vs placebo. So met is the reasonable reading, and the stored evidence states its reliance on effect size openly; not_assessable would be the only alternative. Serious AEs were 3/81 in every arm.

All axes match. COMPLETED, n=1015. The 20 mg dose met all four co-primary comparisons (frequency p=0.0117 and 0.0001; severity p=0.0310 and <.0001). The 15 mg dose met frequency (p=0.0436 and 0.0029) but failed severity (p=0.7786 and 0.7941), so the label is mixed. SAEs were 21/192 (15 mg) and 21/193 (20 mg) against 3/194 on placebo over the same 53-week exposure, driven by endometrial disorder (12/12/0) and endometrial hyperplasia (3/8/0). That is a clear excess on drug, so notable is right. Mixed is not not_met, so efficacy_failure=false.

All axes match. Single-arm open-label study in previously untreated patients (n=33). The only primary outcome is the confirmed inhibitor rate, 3.03% (95% CI 0.08-15.76), a descriptive safety measure with no prespecified threshold or test, so not_assessable fits. There were 23/33 SAEs but no comparator and no deaths; they are mostly typical events for this population (central venous catheterisation 9, falls 5, head injury 3) plus 1 factor IX inhibition, so none_evident.

All axes match. PFS for veliparib + carboplatin/paclitaxel vs placebo + carboplatin/paclitaxel: HR 0.789, p=0.227. Veliparib + TMZ was worse (HR 1.858, p=0.001). Safety: the veliparib + TMZ arm had more all-cause deaths (76/93 vs 65/96) over up to 72 months of follow-up, matching its worse OS (HR 1.512, p=0.017). That reflects a chemo-free regimen's inferior efficacy, not toxicity, and its SAEs were lower (16/93 vs 26/96). Veliparib + carboplatin/paclitaxel: deaths 59/93, SAEs 32/93 vs 26/96. none_evident holds, though notable would be arguable from the death count alone.

All axes match. SDAI remission at week 24: 21.3% vs 16.0%, logistic regression p=0.2359, so not_met in a phase 3 efficacy trial. Borderline safety: Cohort 1 SAEs were 32/451 (7.1%) on abatacept + MTX vs 9/301 (3.0%) on placebo + MTX. Deaths were 1 vs 1, the SAE terms show no clustering, and per-arm exposure over the roughly 54-month window with early escape to open label is not given. A clear excess is not established, so none_evident is defensible.

All axes match. Change in monthly migraine days: both erenumab doses beat placebo (LS mean difference -2.46 and -2.45, both p<0.001). SAEs were 7/282 placebo, 6/190 for 70 mg and 2/188 for 140 mg, with no deaths.

All axes match. Responders weaned off third-line agents: 28/66 placebo vs 29/66 SAGE-547, OR 1.056, p=0.878. Deaths (17/67 vs 12/65) and SAEs (27/67 vs 22/65) were modestly higher on drug, in a critically ill population with high baseline mortality. That is not a clear excess under the rubric, so none_evident is right, though notable would be a borderline alternative. The stored evidence denominators of 66/66 match the posted primary-outcome denominators.

All axes match. 24-month DFS: 89.8% vs 83.8%, HR 0.62 (0.31-1.25), p=0.18. The second primary entry (36-month DFS, 86.7% vs 80.8%) has no posted analysis. The record shows no subgroup analysis, so mixed does not apply. Deaths were 1/136 vs 0/139 and SAEs 14/136 vs 12/139, with no clustering.

All axes match. Change in percent-predicted FVC at week 16: CMK389 -0.48 vs placebo +1.02. Bayesian posterior difference -1.49 (-3.56, 0.60), and the posterior probability that treatment beats placebo is 0.18, so not_met. SAEs were 2/31 vs 0/31 (one head injury, one squamous cell skin carcinoma), with no deaths.

All axes match. Time to exacerbation: median 58 vs 51.5 days, HR 1.33 (0.96-1.84), stratified log-rank p=0.0715, so not significant. SAEs were 21/219 (9.6%) vs 11/110 (10.0%), mostly 'disease progression', with no deaths.

All axes match. This is an immunogenicity study with CHMP/CBER success criteria stated in the outcome descriptions (seroconversion >40%, seroprotection >70%, GMFR >2.5). Day 21 seroconversion was 75/76, 74/75 and 57/58, and GMFR was 25.7 to 32.2, so every criterion was met. not_assessable would be a defensible alternative, since the record has no formal hypothesis test. SAEs were 1/76, 0/75 and 1/58 (dengue fever, influenza), with no deaths.

All axes agree. The record posts no statistical analysis for the primary outcome: placebo 77.8% (n=23) vs BTL TML HSV 45.5% (n=9). The percentages do not even fit the denominators, so the result can't be judged. SAEs were 0/84 on drug vs 2/87 on placebo.

All axes agree. Clinical cure at Day 21 was not met: CMH p=0.6154, RD -5.54 [-21.9, 10.8], numerically favouring control. The AE module shows clearly more harm on AR-105: deaths 25/79 vs 13/79 and SAEs 36/79 vs 22/79.

All axes agree. This is a single-arm phase 1/2 trial. Both primaries are descriptive: grade 4/5 drug-related AEs were 0/3, 0/3 and 0/23, and mucositis grade 1-5 was 1/3, 1/3 and 10/23. There is no comparator or success threshold, and the record's limitations say 'There was no control arm for comparison.' No deaths; 11/23 SAEs in a chemoradiation setting with no comparator.

All axes agree. This is an open-label vaccine extension study of antibody persistence and booster response. All 9 primary outcomes are descriptive (hSBA percentages, GMTs and GMRs). The between-group GMR analyses carry no p-values or hypothesis, and two LLQ primaries say 'Data was not collected for this outcome measure.' Deaths and SAEs were 0 in all arms.

All axes agree under the rubric, with one caveat for downstream users. The posted primary (OR = CR+CRi) is 123/444 vs 38/222, CMH p=0.0024, OR 1.8751. However, the record labels this 'This analysis was exploratory and descriptive' and says the final analysis was run after 574 OS events, so the posted p-value is not the prespecified confirmatory analysis. OS showed no benefit (HR 0.97, p=0.7571). Safety is clearly notable: deaths 138/439 vs 40/222 and SAEs 380/439 vs 163/222. Under the rubric, efficacy_failure=false follows from primary 'met', even though this phase 3 did not improve survival.

All axes agree. Both primaries favour bexagliflozin: 24-h SBP at week 12, LS mean difference -2.72 (p=0.0025), and weeks 24-36, -2.43 (p=0.0117). SAEs were 11/334 vs 10/339 and 9/281 vs 6/281, with no deaths.

All axes agree. The US-registration primary, BCVA gain of 15 letters or more, failed: 48.8% vs 50.5%, p=0.671. The EU-registration primary, macular edema, was met: 5.9% vs 14.3%, p=0.001. That makes the result mixed, so efficacy_failure is false under the rubric. SAEs were 14/293 vs 14/295.

All axes agree. In this single arm, liver Cu at week 48 changed by +92.8 (SE 56.34) ug/g, 2-sided t-test p=0.1002: not significant, and the change was an increase. The brief summary says the main objective was to evaluate this change and to assess efficacy at Week 48. There were 3/31 SAEs, including one drug-induced liver injury, but no deaths and no comparator, so there is no clear excess.

All axes agree. F-VASI50 at week 24 was 3.1% on vehicle vs 25.8-50.0% on ruxolitinib. All four doses beat vehicle significantly (p=0.0057, 0.0243, <0.0001 and 0.0001). No deaths; SAEs were 0 to 4 per arm, with no imbalance in proportion.
